adults.title: The Blessings We Almost Missed
adults.big_idea: When we live the law of tithing, the Lord keeps His promise and opens the windows of heaven, often through significant but subtle blessings that come in His own way and timing.
adults.objective: Learners will name specific, easily overlooked blessings the Lord has given them and feel greater trust to live the law of tithing in faith.
prepare: Read Elder Villanueva's talk, marking paragraphs T30.09–T30.24 (the two sisters and his list) and T30.25–T30.33 (the widow of Zarephath).
Bring paper and pens for everyone.
Write on the board: Malachi 3:10, Doctrine and Covenants 130:20–21, Doctrine and Covenants 58:31, 1 Kings 17:8–16.
Ask six people ahead of time, or as they arrive, to each read one line of Elder Villanueva's list of blessings.
Never ask anyone whether they pay tithing or how their finances are. Keep every question open to all.

segments.name: The promotion that never came
steps: Invite an opening prayer, then tell the story from the talk in your own words: after a sacrament meeting a faithful sister told Elder Villanueva that her testimony of tithing had begun to weaken. She had always paid a full tithe, yet she had never received the promotion she hoped for or the raise she deserved.
Ask the first question below. Give one minute of quiet thought, then two minutes to share with a neighbor. No one needs to report to the class.
Read aloud the first key quote, about the Lord's own way and timing, and write the words way and timing on the board.
questions: When have you kept a commandment and waited for a blessing that did not come the way you pictured?
What does that kind of waiting do to a person's faith?

segments.name: What the Lord actually promised
steps: Divide into groups of three or four. Ask each group to read Malachi 3:10, Doctrine and Covenants 130:20–21 and Doctrine and Covenants 58:31.
Ask the groups to make two short lists: what the Lord promises in these verses, and what He leaves unsaid about the form and the date of the blessing.
Invite one or two groups to share what they noticed. Point out that Elder Villanueva bore his own witness of these verses.
Read the principle Elder Giuffra shared at this conference, one he said his wife often teaches (second aligned quote), and ask the second question.
questions: What does the Lord promise here, and what does He not specify?
How does loving God change the way we wait for a blessing?

segments.name: A little cake first
steps: Explain that Elder Villanueva's mother was providing for eight children during hard financial years when the missionaries taught the law of tithing, and she chose to trust the Lord's promise. Her faith reminds him of the widow of Zarephath.
Read 1 Kings 17:8–16 together, a few verses per reader. Ask everyone to listen for the word first in verse 13.
Read the second key quote, that blessings come after the trial of our faith.
Discuss the questions as a class. Let silence work; wait for answers.
questions: What did the word first ask of the widow, with so little left?
When has the Lord asked you to act before you could see how things would work out? What came afterward?

segments.name: Significant but subtle
steps: Read Elder Bednar's words, quoted in the talk (first aligned quote). Ask: which word in that sentence stands out to you?

Explain that these words prompted Elder Villanueva to make a list, and that the Holy Ghost helped him recognize many blessings. Have your six readers read his list, one line each (T30.14–T30.19): steady employment, good health, home and possessions preserved, ability to manage time and resources to obtain an education, the gift of gratitude, recognizing the Holy Ghost in important decisions.
Tell briefly of the second sister, whose 20-liter (5-gallon) propane tank lasted far longer than she expected. Read Deuteronomy 29:5 and then ask the speaker's own question (third key quote).
Check for understanding: ask one or two people to say in a single sentence what the windows of heaven might look like on an ordinary Tuesday.
questions: Which blessings on Elder Villanueva's list are temporal and which are spiritual? Which would be easiest to overlook?
Why might the Lord often bless us quietly?

segments.name: My own list
steps: Hand out paper. Explain that Elder Villanueva invited the first sister to write her own list of significant yet subtle blessings. Invite the class to try the same thing now.
Give three full minutes of silence. Suggest they pray silently first for the Holy Ghost to help them recognize blessings, as He helped Elder Villanueva. Write alongside them.
Invite everyone to share one line of their list with a neighbor. Then take one or two volunteers for the whole class.
questions: What did you write that you had not noticed before today?

segments.name: Choose and trust
steps: Read the fourth key quote, Elder Villanueva's closing testimony and promise.
Invite each person to choose one thing to do this week from the ideas under Act, and to write it at the bottom of their list.
Bear a brief testimony that Heavenly Father knows our needs and that the Lord keeps His promises.
Follow up next week: begin class by asking who added to their list and what they noticed. Keep it to two minutes.

key_quotes.text: Sometimes we expect the Lord’s blessings to come the way we would wish, rather than in His own way and timing.
Elijah understood that blessings will come after the trial of our faith.
Have you ever asked yourselves whether the Lord has caused your personal possessions to last longer because you have faithfully lived the law of tithing?
When we live the law of tithing, the Lord indeed opens the windows of heaven and pours out His promised blessings

scriptures.use: Read in small groups with the two Doctrine and Covenants passages; list what the Lord promises and what He leaves unsaid about form and timing.
Read in the same groups; ask how this law connects obedience and blessings.
Read aloud together, a few verses each; listen for the word first in verse 13 and discuss what it asked of the widow.
Read after the propane tank story; ask what quiet blessing Israel might have overlooked for forty years.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder David A. Bednar
aligned_quotes.text: As we live the law of tithing, we often receive significant but subtle blessings that are not always what we expect and easily can be overlooked

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Giuffra
aligned_quotes.text: We keep the commandments because we love God, not merely because we hope to receive the blessings that come from obedience.

takeaways: The Lord keeps every promise, in His own way and timing.
The windows of heaven often open quietly; I can ask the Holy Ghost to help me see.
Like the widow, I can put the Lord first and trust that blessings follow faith.
act: Keep your list where you will see it and add one line each night this week.
In prayer, thank Heavenly Father by name for three subtle blessings before asking for anything.
The next time income arrives, pay tithing first, before other spending, as an act of trust.
Tell a family member or friend about one blessing you had overlooked.
music: Because I Have Been Given Much
adapt: At home: do the list at the table, each person writing three lines, then read them to each other. Skip the group reading and read only Malachi 3:10 and 1 Kings 17:13–16.
Large class: keep every discussion in pairs or threes and take only two comments per question from the whole room.
Short on time: keep the opening story, Elder Bednar's words, the list reading and the silent writing. Those four parts carry the lesson.

youth.title: Hidden in Plain Sight
youth.big_idea: The Lord keeps His promise to bless those who live the law of tithing, but His blessings are often subtle and come in His way and timing, so we have to learn to see them.
youth.objective: Youth will explain what the Lord does and does not promise in Malachi 3:10 and will start their own list of subtle blessings they had overlooked.
prepare: Read Elder Villanueva's talk, especially T30.09–T30.24 and the widow of Zarephath in T30.25–T30.33.
Bring paper and pens; youth will also use their scriptures or the Gospel Library app.
Write on the board: Malachi 3:10 and 1 Kings 17:8–16.
Have a timer ready (a phone works).
Do not ask anyone whether they or their family pay tithing.

segments.name: You see what you look for
steps: As soon as the prayer ends, say: you have twenty seconds to silently find everything green in this room. Go.
When time is up, have everyone close their eyes. Ask them to name things in the room that are brown. Let them laugh at how little they remember.
Ask the question below, then say that today's talk is about blessings that are in plain sight and easy to miss.
questions: Why did you miss the brown things when they were right in front of you?

segments.name: The honest question
steps: Tell the story from the talk: a faithful sister told Elder Villanueva her testimony of tithing was weakening. She had always paid a full tithe but never got the promotion she hoped for or the raise she deserved.
Ask the first question and let youth answer honestly. Do not correct yet.
Have everyone open Malachi 3:10 on a phone or in scriptures. In pairs, give one minute to find what the Lord promises and one thing the verse never says.
Hear from two or three pairs. Read Doctrine and Covenants 58:31 (fourth key quote), then the first key quote about the Lord's own way and timing.
questions: Is she wrong to feel that way? What would you say to her?
Does this verse promise money? What does it promise?

segments.name: First, not last
steps: Explain that Elder Villanueva was ten when his family was baptized. Money was tight; his mother was working tirelessly to support eight children. When the missionaries taught tithing, she chose to trust the Lord's promise. Her faith makes him think of a widow in the Old Testament.
Form teams of three or four. Each team reads 1 Kings 17:8–16 and writes a headline of ten words or fewer that captures the story. Give four minutes on the timer.
Teams read their headlines aloud. The class votes by applause for the one that best captures the story; a team cannot vote for itself.
Read the second key quote, then ask the questions.
questions: Elijah asked her to make his portion first. Why does the order matter?
What is hard about giving to the Lord first when you do not have much?

segments.name: Blessing hunt
steps: Read Elder Bednar's words, quoted in the talk (first aligned quote). Ask youth to say the two words that describe these blessings: significant and subtle.

Explain that those words moved Elder Villanueva to make a list, and that the Holy Ghost helped him recognize blessings: steady work, good health for his family, home and possessions preserved, being able to manage time and resources to get an education, the gift of gratitude, and recognizing the Holy Ghost when making important decisions. Add the sister whose 20-liter propane tank lasted far longer than she expected.
Same teams, three minutes on the timer: list subtle blessings a person your age could easily overlook. Specific beats general: a friend who saved me a seat on Monday counts; friends does not.
Teams read their lists. Give a point for every item no other team wrote. Congratulate the winners.
Check for understanding: ask one youth to explain in their own words why a blessing can be both significant and easy to miss.

segments.name: My list
steps: Explain that Elder Villanueva invited the sister to write her own list. Invite youth to try it now, alone and in silence, on paper or in the notes app on their phones.
Suggest they begin with a silent prayer asking the Holy Ghost to help them recognize blessings. Give three minutes. Write your own list too.
Invite anyone who wants to share one line to do so. Share one of yours.
questions: What is on your list that you had not thought of as a blessing before?

segments.name: Choose one
steps: Read the third key quote: the Lord gives commandments because He wants us to receive His blessings. Then read Elder Giuffra's words from this conference (second aligned quote).
Invite each youth to choose one idea under Act and tell the person next to them which one.
Bear a short testimony that Heavenly Father knows them and keeps His promises.
Follow up next week: start class by asking who kept their list going and what surprised them.

key_quotes.text: Sometimes we expect the Lord’s blessings to come the way we would wish, rather than in His own way and timing.
Elijah understood that blessings will come after the trial of our faith.
He gives us commandments because He wants us to receive His blessings.
Who am I, saith the Lord, that have promised and have not fulfilled?

scriptures.use: Read in pairs on phones or in scriptures; find what the Lord promises and one thing the verse never says.
Teams read the story and write a headline of ten words or fewer; then discuss why Elijah asked the widow to give first.
Read aloud after pairs report on Malachi 3:10 (it is the fourth key quote); ask how they would answer the Lord's question.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder David A. Bednar
aligned_quotes.text: As we live the law of tithing, we often receive significant but subtle blessings that are not always what we expect and easily can be overlooked

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Giuffra
aligned_quotes.text: the law of tithing is a law of faith

takeaways: The Lord always keeps His promises, in His way and on His timing.
Many of my biggest blessings are quiet ones I have to look for.
Giving to the Lord first is how I show I trust Him.
act: Add one line to your blessings list every night this week before you go to sleep.
The next time you earn or receive money, set aside tithing first, before you spend any of it. If you are not sure how to pay it, ask a parent or a member of the bishopric.
Read 1 Kings 17:8–16 again on your own and thank Heavenly Father in prayer for one thing in your life that has not run out.
Tell one person about a blessing you nearly missed.
adapt: At home or with two or three youth: skip the teams. Write headlines and blessing lists individually and compare.
Large class: use more teams of four and hear only the best two items from each team's list.
Short on time: keep the green and brown opener, Malachi 3:10 in pairs, Elder Bednar's words and the personal list.

children.title: Heavenly Father Keeps His Promises
children.big_idea: When I pay tithing I show Heavenly Father that I trust Him, and He keeps His promise to bless me.
children.objective: Children will say that Heavenly Father keeps His promises and will draw blessings He has given them.
prepare: Bring ten building blocks (or ten paper circles), an empty bowl, an empty cup, a flashlight, paper and crayons.
Cut five paper hearts. On each, write or draw one blessing: a healthy body, a home, learning, a thankful heart, the Holy Ghost. Hide them around the room in easy places before class.
Read 1 Kings 17:8–16 so you can tell the story in your own simple words.
The truth to repeat all lesson long: Heavenly Father keeps His promises.

segments.name: Sing and say
steps: Sing one verse of Keep the Commandments together, then invite a child to pray.
Teach the truth for today with actions: point up for Heavenly Father, hug yourself for keeps, hold out both hands for His promises. Say it together three times, getting quieter each time.
Tell the children that Elder Villanueva spoke at general conference about a promise Heavenly Father makes to us.

segments.name: Ten blocks
steps: Tell the children that when Elder Villanueva was ten years old, his family was baptized and learned about tithing.
Let the children count ten blocks out loud as you stack them. Move one block to the side. Explain: tithing is giving one part out of ten back to Heavenly Father. It is a way to say, I trust Thee.
Let each child have a turn counting ten and moving the tithing block.
Explain that Elder Villanueva's mother did not have very much, but she chose to trust the Lord's promise and pay tithing. Say the truth together again with actions.
questions: How do you think Heavenly Father feels when we trust Him?

segments.name: The bowl that did not run out
steps: Choose children to be Elijah, the widow and her son. Everyone else gathers sticks by picking up crayons from around the room, the way the widow was gathering sticks.

Tell the story simply while the children act it out with the empty bowl and cup: the widow had only a little flour and a little oil left. The prophet Elijah asked her to make some bread for him first. He promised that her flour and oil would not run out.
Have the widow pretend to make bread and carry it to Elijah first. Then let every child peek in the bowl as you say: day after day, there was still enough. The Lord kept His promise.
Say the truth together with actions. If time allows, act it again with new actors.
questions: Was it easy or hard for the widow to share first?
What did Heavenly Father do for her?

segments.name: Flashlight blessing hunt
steps: Explain that Heavenly Father promises to open the windows of heaven for those who pay tithing. Many of His blessings are quiet, so we have to look for them.
Dim the lights if you can. Give one child the flashlight to search for a hidden heart while the others point and help. Take turns until all five hearts are found.
Each time a heart is found, read the blessing and have everyone open their arms wide like a window and say, thank you, Heavenly Father.
Tell the children that Elder Villanueva made a list of blessings like these, and the Holy Ghost helped him see them.

segments.name: My window of blessings
steps: Give each child paper and crayons. Help them fold the paper in half twice and open it to make a window with four parts.
Invite them to draw one blessing from Heavenly Father in each part. Remind them of quiet blessings: a body that can run, a warm bed, someone who loves them, a good feeling from the Holy Ghost.
Walk around and ask each child to tell you about one drawing. Check for understanding by asking: who gave you that blessing?

segments.name: Share and choose
steps: Sit in a circle. Roll or pass a block to each child in turn; the child holding it shows one drawing and names the blessing.
Read the first key quote slowly, then say it simply: Heavenly Father gives us commandments because He wants to bless us.
Invite each child to choose one thing to do this week from the ideas under Act. Say the truth one last time with actions and bear a short testimony that Heavenly Father knows and loves each child.
Send the drawings home. Follow up next week by asking: what blessings did you find this week?

key_quotes.text: He gives us commandments because He wants us to receive His blessings.
God is our loving Heavenly Father.
When we live the law of tithing, the Lord indeed opens the windows of heaven

scriptures.use: Tell the story of the widow and Elijah in your own simple words while the children act it out with an empty bowl and cup.
Before the flashlight hunt, show the verse in your scriptures and explain that the Lord promises to open the windows of heaven.
While children draw, tell them this verse teaches that Heavenly Father knows what we need even before we ask.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Giuffra
aligned_quotes.text: the law of tithing is a law of faith

takeaways: Paying tithing shows that I trust Him.
I can look for quiet blessings and say thank you.
act: Show your window drawing to someone at home and tell them about one blessing.
Each night this week, thank Heavenly Father in your prayer for one blessing you noticed that day.
When you receive money, count out your tithing first with a grown-up's help.

adapt.younger: Ages 3–7: keep each part short and repeat the truth with actions between every activity. Count the ten blocks together as a group, let a helper hold the flashlight with the child, and draw just one big blessing instead of four. Act out the widow story twice so more children have a turn.
adapt.older: Ages 8–11: have a child read Malachi 3:10 aloud and another read 1 Kings 17:16. Let an older child lead the ten-block counting or narrate the widow story. Ask: why might Heavenly Father send blessings that are quiet and easy to miss? Invite them to write a list of five blessings on the back of their window.
